extracted.intended_audience: judges, lawyers, agency officials, litigants, and others interested in administrative law and judicial review
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and scope by which a reviewing court examines agency actions under the Administrative Procedure Act §706, including grounds for setting aside agency decisions and the record-review rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decide relevant questions of law and interpret provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent necessary to decision and when presented, the reviewing court shall decide all relevant questions of law, interpret constitutional and statutory provisions, and determine the meaning or applicability of the terms of an agency action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clause conditions judicial review on necessity and presentation; courts resolve legal questions and statutory/constitutional interpretation implicated by agency actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compel agency action unlawfully withheld or unreasonably delayed
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) compel agency action unlawfully withheld or unreasonably delayed;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts may order agencies to perform a nondiscretionary duty or remedy unreasonable delay in agency decisionmaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set aside action that is arbitrary, capricious, an abuse of discretion, or otherwise not in accordance with law
rubrics_metrics.description: (2)(A) hold unlawful and set aside agency action, findings, and conclusions found to be— arbitrary, capricious, an abuse of discretion, or otherwise not in accordance with law;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The familiar 'arbitrary and capricious' standard governs many informal rulemakings and other agency actions; courts examine reasoned decisionmaking, consideration of relevant factors, and rational connection between facts and choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set aside action contrary to constitutional right, power, privilege, or immunity
rubrics_metrics.description: (2)(B) hold unlawful and set aside agency action, findings, and conclusions found to be— contrary to constitutional right, power, privilege, or immunity;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency actions that violate constitutional provisions or infringe protected rights are subject to invalidation under this clause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set aside action in excess of statutory jurisdiction, authority, or limitations, or short of statutory right
rubrics_metrics.description: (2)(C) hold unlawful and set aside agency action, findings, and conclusions found to be— in excess of statutory jurisdiction, authority, or limitations, or short of statutory right;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts assess whether agencies acted within the bounds of statutory grants of authority and complied with statutory limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set aside action without observance of procedure required by law
rubrics_metrics.description: (2)(D) hold unlawful and set aside agency action, findings, and conclusions found to be— without observance of procedure required by law;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural defects (e.g., failure to follow notice-and-comment requirements where applicable) can render agency action unlawful and subject to vacatur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set aside action unsupported by substantial evidence (on the record)
rubrics_metrics.description: (2)(E) hold unlawful and set aside agency action, findings, and conclusions found to be— unsupported by substantial evidence in a case subject to sections 556 and 557 of this title or otherwise reviewed on the record of an agency hearing provided by statute;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In formal adjudications or cases reviewed on the agency hearing record, courts apply the substantial-evidence standard—assessing whether the record contains such relevant evidence as a reasonable mind might accept as adequate to support the agency's conclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set aside action unwarranted by the facts where trial de novo applies
rubrics_metrics.description: (2)(F) hold unlawful and set aside agency action, findings, and conclusions found to be— unwarranted by the facts to the extent that the facts are subject to trial de novo by the reviewing court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the facts are subject to trial de novo, courts may set aside agency findings that the evidence does not support on fresh factfinding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review the whole record and apply rule of prejudicial error
rubrics_metrics.description: In making the foregoing determinations, the court shall review the whole record or those parts of it cited by a party, and due account shall be taken of the rule of prejudicial error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts must review the full administrative record (or cited portions) and consider whether any legal or procedural errors were prejudicial to the outcome before setting aside agency action.
